- **Cheaper** than vector RAG: for both index and query.
- **Faster**: trees are created from layout stats.
- **Unified** SDK: vectorless RAG. **Local** or **cloud**, for index and chat.
- Runs on your **Claude subscription**.

Index, to chat, to agent integration, one client.
Local mode needs no server, no vector DB, no PageIndex API key.

```python
client = PageIndexClient()
client.submit_document("report.pdf")
client.chat("What does the report conclude?")
```

## Highlights

- **Flash engine**: the local default (`mode="standard"` keeps the classic LLM pipeline). Embedded bookmarks are consumed when trustworthy, and tree optimization is on by default — `optimize="merge"` for the deterministic LLM-free pass, `"full"` (default) adds LLM expand, which runs a wave of nodes concurrently instead of one round-trip at a time.
- **One complete surface, local and cloud**: `PageIndexLocalClient(storage_path=...)` is the same client as cloud — submit, tree, page content, chat, and agent tools all present in both modes, so code moves between them unchanged.
- **Cloud documents, your own model**: `api_key` decides where your documents live; a configured chat model decides who answers — and the two combine. `PageIndexClient(api_key="pi-...", chat_model="openai/gpt-5.2")` runs the same in-process document-QA engine over the live cloud tool set. Page content flows through your process to your provider on your credentials; `doc_id` targets at the prompt level; `enable_citations` stays with the managed chat.
- **Agent integration**: the cloud MCP tool contract, in-process — `client.agent_tools()` (plain functions), `as_openai_tools()`, `as_anthropic_tools()`, `as_claude_mcp()`, plus one-call `openai_agent_config()` / `anthropic_runner_config()` / `claude_agent_config()` bundles and `agent_instructions()` for the system prompt. Eigent v1.0.8 brings a new way to move around the app — a rail with Home and Settings, a Home that lists every Space and its Sessions, and search across everything — and makes the new conversation timeline the default, with the agent's work told as a readable task log.

This update also fixes a long list of bugs found in testing and reported by the community, from deleting Spaces and choosing folders to tool calls that stopped a task.

### Highlights

- **A rail with Home and Settings** — A slim column on the left holds Home, your pinned Spaces, Settings and your account. Pin a Space to keep it one click away.
- **Home lists every Space and its Sessions** — Open, start, pin, rename, end or delete a Session straight from Home. Right-click a Session for its menu, and see at a glance which Sessions have news you haven't read.
- **Search everything** — Press ⌘K or the Search button in the top bar to find Spaces, Sessions, Tasks, files, Automations and Dispatch, in any Space.
- **Back and Forward** — Move back and forward between Home, Spaces, Sessions and Settings from the top bar.
- **The new conversation timeline is the default** — The agent's work reads as a task log, approvals and questions sit in the conversation and name the file or command they are for, and a divider shows when the model changes. Choose how much detail you see.
- **A new composer** — One "+" button adds files, Skills and Connectors, with a single search across all three. Connectors show their logo and name in your message, and a short welcome helps you start your first Session.
- **An emoji for each Space** — Give a Space an emoji instead of its first letter. The emoji picker works offline.

### Spaces and files

- A Space can use a folder outside your home folder. System folders are still refused, and a Task in a Space set to your whole home folder is refused up front with a note on how to continue.
- A Space that still has Sessions can be deleted.

OpenShip 1.0 brings a refreshed dashboard, edge maintenance and custom pages,
deploy links, and scheduled mail workflows. Includes every change since 0.9.12,
with more reliable builds, imports, billing and recovery.

**Recommended update:** administrators should update all OpenShip components. This
release closes an authorization flaw that allowed ordinary organization members
to invoke administrative operations, including host command execution.

### Security and access

- **Administrative authorization** — Require administrative authority across HTTP, SDK,
  native and MCP access. Scoped tokens remain bounded by their owner's current organization
  role, including after demotion. Preserve explicitly delegated, resource-scoped
  administration (#1783, #1784).
- **Hostname sign-in** — Choose a sign-in page or the browser's native authentication prompt
  for self-hosted hostnames. Customize sign-in HTML and session duration, revoke sessions,
  and see enabled protection directly on domain cards.
- **Actions tracing** — Update the Actions worker to OpenTelemetry 1.47.0, fixing bypassed
  attribute-length limits in its tracing dependency.
- **Release build isolation** — Keep generated local mail credentials and runtime caches out
  of image build contexts. Bundle the shared assistant client and its dependency patch so
  release builds do not depend on a sibling checkout or baked development URLs.
- **Website image verification** — Include the website's client-message generator in its
  Docker build, and verify the production website image and its public pages before release.

### Edge pages and routing

- **Edge maintenance** — Serve maintenance HTML directly from the edge while the application
  keeps running. Restore normal routing when maintenance is disabled.
- **Custom error pages** — Upload HTML pages and assign error statuses, with server defaults
  and project or hostname overrides. Customize unmatched-host and direct-IP pages.
- **Authentication header limits*

### Fixed

- **`run verify` has no unit cliff for mixed Chinese/English reports (#71, reported by @redmyapple).** Length and citation density switched from whitespace words to characters / 3 at a spaceless-script ratio of exactly 0.3, so a mixed report 0.1% under the cutoff was measured at about a third of its length and blocked on `length-in-range`, while ~600 more characters of Chinese made the same report pass. Across a band from 0.2 to 0.4 the count now blends linearly between the two measures, and so does the length target. Text below 0.2 (English, Korean) and above 0.4 (Chinese, Japanese, Thai) is counted exactly as before. A blended check says so in its detail (`mixed script, N% counted as chars / 3`).
- **Generated instructions no longer prefix commands with `PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8` (#205, reported by @vik-borisov).** That is bash syntax; Windows PowerShell reads `PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8` as a command name and fails before hyperresearch starts, and every reinstall wrote the prefix back into the fetcher, cite-checker, corpus-critic, draft-orchestrator, source-analyst and browser-fetcher agents and steps 2 and 8. The prefix was never needed: on Windows the CLI already switches its own stdout and stderr to UTF-8 at startup. A test installs both targets and checks that no installed instruction carries the prefix.
- **Install no longer deletes a user's own `hyperresearch-*` skill folder (#206, from @ray910408).** The step-skill prunes treated any `SKILL.md` that mentions hyperresearch as ours, so a hand-written `.claude/skills/hyperresearch-my-notes/` (or a `~/.claude/skills/hyperresearch-2024-...` under `--global`) was deleted with everything in it. A prefix-matched folder is now removed only when its `SKILL.md` carries the rendered-install provenance header or its name is a step the package ships.

### Security

- Cloud-agent tools enforce the bot's current integration assignments and allowed tools before using a connected account.
- Inbound email needs signed recipients before it can be treated as the owner's instructions; an SPF pass reported by a relay is no longer enough. Email routines can still accept signed mail as outside data ([inbound email](docs/self-host-inbound-email.md#who-can-start-work)).
- Saving memory after reading outside content follows the run's approval mode and **Always allow** list, including after a run resumes ([approvals](docs/approvals.md)).
- Spoken answers containing both yes and no cannot approve an action. A texted YES or NO applies only to a group invite or agent connection request delivered before the reply.
- Ambiguous checkout totals require manual payment, including when an approved action is checked again. Amounts such as `$.99` are read as cents, and payment-method controls are excluded from purchase approval.
- Model connection errors and logs hide more credential formats, including quoted and encoded values, custom headers, URL passwords, cookies and nested JSON. Card redaction also covers grouped American Express and Diners Club numbers.
- Team-chat sender and channel names cannot escape their prompt labels. Malformed stored approval, plugin and billing configuration is rejected, and unexpected internal errors are no longer shown as client error details.
- Removing connections and replaced secrets retries external cleanup after temporary failures. Desktop tool servers keep sign-in cookies separate from each other and the app, and disconnecting clears that server's browser.
- Native clipboard writes require HTTPS or a loopback origin. App sign-in links reject malformed addresses and non-web schemes before reaching native handlers.
- Private memory endpoints, including loopback addresses, require operator consent at the adapter boundary as well as the API.
- Billing database triggers resist temporary-object shadowing,

Maintenance and security release.

- **Minimum Python is now 3.11** (was 3.10). Python 3.10 reached end of life in October 2026, and the patched releases of our optional and transitive dependencies no longer ship wheels for it. Raising the floor lets the lockfile move to those patched versions. Installs on Python 3.10 keep resolving to 0.9.110, the last 3.10-compatible release; everyone on 3.11 and up is unaffected.
- **Security:** with 3.10 dropped, the committed lockfile resolves Pillow 13.0.0, filelock 4.2.4 and opentelemetry-api 1.45.2 for every supported interpreter, clearing the open Dependabot advisories against the older pins. Pillow is only pulled in by the optional `svg`/`all` extras, not the core install. This is a dependency and packaging change only: no change to extraction behaviour and the AST cache schema is unchanged.
- **Test:** the backtick-substitution runtime tests now skip on bash older than 4.1 (they rely on `BASH_XTRACEFD`, added in 4.1) instead of misbehaving on the bash 3.2 that macOS ships.

## Safer credentials and upgrades, background Library downloads, and configurable sampling

2.0.1 is a maintenance release with many security and reliability fixes. A few of them change behavior that existing deployments may depend on, so check the upgrade notes below before upgrading.

### ⚠️ Before you upgrade

- **API keys set through environment variables now only go to environment-configured endpoints** (#8265). An API key set through an `LDR_*` variable is sent only to the URL set through the matching `LDR_*` variable, or to the provider's default endpoint. It is no longer sent to a URL saved in account settings.
  - **What to do:** if you set a key through the environment and a custom endpoint through the Settings UI, also set the endpoint through the environment, for example `LDR_LLM_OPENAI_ENDPOINT_URL`.
  - **If you don't:** LLM calls, model discovery, embeddings and Paperless will fail or report nothing available.
  - Settings and Research now show an inline warning when this conflict is detected (#8675).
- **`LDR_LLM_REQUIRE_LOCAL_ENDPOINT=enabled` and `LDR_EMBEDDINGS_REQUIRE_LOCAL=enabled` are now enforced.** Previously the egress policy read `enabled` as off, so cloud providers were silently allowed. Check that no deployment with these set relies on a cloud LLM or embedding provider.
- **OpenAI-compatible chat calls no longer follow HTTP redirects** (#8259). A 3xx response from the configured endpoint now fails the call. If your endpoint redirects, configure its final URL instead.
- **Databases are not migrated without a pre-migration backup** (#8366). If the backup cannot be written, sign-in is refused and the data is left unchanged. The most common cause is less than twice the database's size in free disk space; some bind mounts that reject permission changes also cause it. The server log gives the reason.
  - **What to do:** fix the cause and sign in again.
  - **Last resort:** make your own copy of the data directory, then set `LDR_BOOTSTRAP_ALLOW_

- **Cheaper** than vector RAG: for both index and query.
- **Faster**: trees are created from layout stats.
- **Unified** SDK: vectorless RAG. **Local** or **cloud**, for index and chat.
- Runs on your **Claude subscription**.

Index, to chat, to agent integration, one client.
Local mode needs no server, no vector DB, no PageIndex API key.

```python
client = PageIndexClient()
client.submit_document("report.pdf")
client.chat("What does the report conclude?")
```

## Highlights

- **Flash engine**: the local default (`mode="standard"` keeps the classic LLM pipeline). Embedded bookmarks are consumed when trustworthy, and tree optimization is on by default — `optimize="merge"` for the deterministic LLM-free pass, `"full"` (default) adds LLM expand, which runs a wave of nodes concurrently instead of one round-trip at a time.
- **One complete surface, local and cloud**: `PageIndexLocalClient(storage_path=...)` is the same client as cloud — submit, tree, page content, chat, and agent tools all present in both modes, so code moves between them unchanged.
- **Cloud documents, your own model**: `api_key` decides where your documents live; a configured chat model decides who answers — and the two combine. `PageIndexClient(api_key="pi-...", chat_model="openai/gpt-5.2")` runs the same in-process document-QA engine over the live cloud tool set. Page content flows through your process to your provider on your credentials; `doc_id` targets at the prompt level; `enable_citations` stays with the managed chat.
- **Agent integration**: the cloud MCP tool contract, in-process — `client.agent_tools()` (plain functions), `as_openai_tools()`, `as_anthropic_tools()`, `as_claude_mcp()`, plus one-call `openai_agent_config()` / `anthropic_runner_config()` / `claude_agent_config()` bundles and `agent_instructions()` for the system prompt. Cloud clients get the live server tool set over the MCP bridge (read-only endpoint by default); local clients get the in-process subset with the same schemas

## Highlights

### Code lessons alongside your source (#753) — by @06FallingLight90

The code viewer now includes per-file explanations aligned with the guided tour. Tour-covered files get detailed sections; clicking a section highlights its source lines. Other files receive an overview. Lessons are generated when the tour is built or rebuilt, published after the graph is saved, and pruned when files leave the graph. Partial updates preserve existing lessons; a tour rebuild refreshes their line ranges.

### Devin support and a stdio MCP server (#726) — by @isaiahfrantz

Devin can load the plugin's analysis pipeline and post-commit hooks. The new MCP server exposes six tools for existing graphs: status, search, explanation, change-impact analysis, onboarding, and dashboard startup. Each tool includes graph freshness information, and dashboard processes are stopped when the server exits. Setup instructions are in the [MCP README](https://github.com/Egonex-AI/Understand-Anything/blob/v2.9.8/understand-anything-plugin/packages/mcp/README.md).

### Incremental analysis and symbol preservation

- Deterministic incremental preparation reconciles file changes, ignore rules, structural fingerprints, and imports. Updates preserve surviving architecture and tour content when those stages do not need to run (#682).
- Source-evidence checks protect existing symbols during incremental updates, and failed finalization restores the saved graph and fingerprints (#683, #753).
- Fingerprints match methods by their enclosing owner and name, keeping same-named methods in different classes distinct (#766) — by @thejesh23.
- Baseline batch merging, Python relative imports, Makefile target detection, and `tested_by` relationships for Swift, Rust, Ruby, and PHP receive correctness fixes (#564, #728, #725, #689).

### Graph freshness and automatic updates

- The dashboard and graph-consuming skills report when saved analysis is stale (#558) — by @jiang4wqy.

Community release: 36 pull requests from 8 contributors, two new extensions, and the local
proxy opt-in promised in v2.6.1.

**After updating, check these if you script against the tool:**

- **IndexNow requires an exact host match.** A URL on a subdomain of the declared host is no
  longer submitted.
- **Exit codes:** `preload_check.py` and `parasite_risk.py` exit with code 1 when no page
  could be fetched, instead of scoring an error page.
- **`seo_updates.py --limit 0` means no limit.** It returned an empty list before.
- **Drift baselines for URLs with path parameters** (`;name=value`) need re-capturing.
- **Audit reports are named `SEO-Audit-Report-*`.**

### New

- **Local proxy opt-in** (#398 by @eduardopicazzo, issue #280). `CLAUDE_SEO_TRUSTED_PROXIES`
  names a proxy on loopback or a private address that you trust, as `host:port`. Fetches,
  screenshots, rendering and Unlighthouse then work in Claude Code cloud sessions and behind
  tools such as cntlm or px. Every destination is still checked before the proxy is asked
  for it, link-local and metadata addresses stay refused, and without the variable nothing
  changes.
- **Shopify extension** (`/seo shopify`, #302 by @Nordalux): a sitemap-complete crawl of a
  store you administer, signed with the store's Crawler Access signature, handed to the
  audit.
- **PostHog extension** (`/seo posthog`, #336 by @AlexMili): organic traffic, landing pages,
  device and country splits from the PostHog MCP server, as a GA4 alternative or complement.
- **Per-project credentials** (#341 by @lciolecki): `CLAUDE_SEO_PROFILE_DIR` points the
  Google, backlink and Matomo credential files at a per-project directory.
- **`/seo bing`, `/seo shopify` and `/seo posthog` load on plugin installs** (issue #458).
  The skills ship with the plugin and the installers only do configuration there.

### Fixed

- **29 correctness fixes by @Afloat16** across reports, drift, schema, transport grading,
  DataForSEO, preload, sitemap, CrUX, Sea

body:
Security release: ten reports from eight researchers, six distinct problems, all
fixed. No new commands.

**After updating, three things behave differently:**

- **Chromium runs sandboxed where the system allows it.** On systems that
  cannot start the sandbox (Ubuntu 23.10 and later, GitHub's Ubuntu runners,
  most Docker images, root)
  pages still render, a warning says why, and the JSON result carries
  `sandbox: false`. The sandbox is best effort unless you set
  `CLAUDE_SEO_CHROMIUM_REQUIRE_SANDBOX=1`, which fails instead.
- **Google sign-in is read-only by default.** A new sign-in asks for read-only
  Search Console and Analytics access. To use `indexing_notify.py`, sign in with
  `google_auth.py --auth --indexing`. Existing sign-ins keep working.
- **Screenshots and rendering no longer use a proxy on a local or private
  address**, and SOCKS or `https://` proxy URLs are refused for browser
  commands. An `http://` proxy on a public address is supported (tested against
  a simulated proxy only). If direct access is allowed, unset the proxy
  variables or use `NO_PROXY` for the audited host. An opt-in for a named local
  proxy is planned for the next release.

Also: `google_auth.py --tier` no longer lists the Indexing API for a read-only
sign-in, and `verify_release.py` now prints manifest values in quotes and fails
on an empty manifest.

### Security

- **The headless browser can no longer be redirected to local addresses**
  (GHSA-8wrm-4mmq-6fx3 by @namaserajesh, GHSA-9pc7-p6cr-942h by @Nordalux, who
  also wrote the initial fix). The earlier guard checked only the first URL of
  a request, so an audited site could redirect Chromium to loopback, private
  network or cloud metadata addresses and have the response returned in the
  audit. Every browser connection now goes through a local guard that checks
  each destination, including every redirect, and connects only to the
  addresses it checked. The guard accepts only the browser it started. Unlighthouse
name: v2.6.1: security fixes

Univer 1.5.0 adds dedicated chart sheets, stacked line charts, and error bars. Pro's free tier now covers more editing and local output workflows. This release also reduces memory use during formula calculation, adds controls for Sheets interactions and Board layout, and improves Office file compatibility.

## New features

### Chart sheets, stacked line charts, and error bars

Give a chart its own tab while keeping its source cells in regular worksheets in the same workbook. Move charts between sheets with undo and redo. With the Sheets Chart Facade loaded, use `workbook.insertChartSheet(info, { name, index })` to set the tab name and zero-based position, and `getPrimaryChart()` to access the main chart. A chart sheet can also continuously fit its main chart to the viewport using `zoomToFit`. Older snapshots without this setting use fixed zoom. [Chart sheets guide](https://docs.univer.ai/guides/sheets/features/charts#chart-sheets)

Create stacked and 100% stacked line charts. The chart editor and the builder and live chart APIs also support per-series error bars for basic 2D column, bar, line, and scatter charts. Use `setErrorBars()` and `clearErrorBars()` to control direction, end caps, styling, and error amounts. Supported amounts include fixed values, percentages, standard deviation, standard error, and positive or negative values from custom fields in the chart's data source. Scatter charts support separate X and Y error bars. [Error bars guide](https://docs.univer.ai/guides/sheets/features/charts#error-bars)

### Editable Board diagrams and a dedicated LaTeX package

Use `planLayout()` to arrange a diagram or adjust connector routes, endpoints, labels, and text fitting. Inspect the returned diagnostics before applying a ready plan with `applyLayoutPlan()`. Applying a plan is undoable, and the resulting shapes and connectors remain editable. Imported tree branches can be collapsed or expanded with `setTreeBranchCollapsed()`. Rendered analysis report

body:
Changes since 1.25.2:

- Keep strikethroughs on pages that strike several lines of similar width, as tracked-changes documents do: the repeated-ruling filter only kept such a rule when it underlined the row it fits, so every one of these strikes was dropped as a table ruling. A rule that snugly strikes through one row is now kept, and the underlined row and the struck row are judged apart so neighbouring rows never combine into one owner (#663).
- Keep strikethroughs on text inside a detected table: clearing the decorations of table text exists for underlines, which a cell's bottom border imitates, and no border runs through a cell's glyphs (#663).
- Emit the strikethroughs recovered above as `<s>` without changing anything else on the page: run merging and heuristic table detection read them as before, and a word hyphenated across a line break inside a struck run rejoins across the reopened `<s>` tag (#663).
- Read a TrueType subset with no `cmap`, no glyph names and no ToUnicode that comes from a core Windows font through the Windows variant of the standard glyph order, which the font's own advances choose: `“N/A”` no longer reads as `—N/A“`, `company’s` as `company‘s` or en dashes as `œ`. A glyph past the standard order that paints nothing but advances reads as a space, so Word's justified Arial lines no longer read U+FFFD between every word (#618).

API: `TextItem::layout_strikeout` (Rust), the strikeout layout heuristics read. It equals `is_strikeout` except on the strikethroughs recovered above. Rust literals of `TextItem` must include the new field. The Node, Python and WebAssembly bindings and the `pdf2md --items-json` fields are unchanged.

Release preparation: #665.

[Full changelog](https://github.com/firecrawl/pdf-inspector/compare/v1.25.2...v1.26.0)

Agent Skills 0.6.16 lets specs evolve past V1, teaches the docs skill to spot drift, stops the frontend skill from installing toolchains just to verify, and fixes two quality-gate examples that could never fail.

## Skills

- **Spec evolution** (#383, @ayobamiseun). Specs now carry a version and an Out of Scope (Deferred) list, and a change to a shipped feature gets its own small delta spec (`SPEC-<change>.md`) instead of a rewrite. `/spec` writes one when `SPEC.md` already exists, and `/build auto` picks the delta that isn't `Status: implemented` and refuses to run a plan generated from a different spec.
- **Documentation drift** (#514, @vyasdx). When a doc may be stale, documentation-and-adrs compares the last commit to the code with the last commit to the doc, and says "can't tell" instead of "current" when the history is unordered. Change logs are appended to, never rewritten.
- **Verify with what the project has** (#732, @TwelveNights). frontend-ui-engineering no longer installs a test runner or type checker just to check its work, and follows the WAI-ARIA APG patterns for menus, dialogs, tabs, listboxes and comboboxes. Measured +0.10 across 11 models, with package installs down from 24% to 4% of runs.
- **Review findings checked against the code** (#736, @CybotTM). code-review-and-quality checks each finding against the callers, guards and tests that reach the change, labels defects already in the base separately, and treats zero findings as a valid result.
- **Gates that can fail** (#786, @rudycelekli). `depcruise --validate src` printed usage and exited 0; the constraints skill now runs `depcruise src`.
- **Session secret** (#787, @rudycelekli). The hardening example fails at startup when `SESSION_SECRET` is missing instead of returning 500 on every request.
- **OWASP Top 10:2025** (#785, @usaid7015). The checklist and security skill use the 2025 numbering, cited with the year.
- **Skills fire on pasted code** (#762, #763, #757, @ayobamiseun, part of #620).
name: Agent Skills 0.6.16
